name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Overlooks the Tawang Chu valley with a 28-foot gilded Buddha statue and ancient manuscripts.
facts: Birthplace connection to the 6th Dalai Lama

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at about 4170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang with Sela Lake, snow cover much of the year, and panoramic Himalayan views. Sela Tunnel provides all-weather access.
facts: On NH-13 connecting Tawang to the rest of India
Border between Tawang and West Kameng; Source: Wikipedia

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake formed by an earthquake, famous for upright dead tree trunks in the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot. On the route toward Bum La Pass.
facts: Formed by earthquake submerging a forest
Army permit often required for access

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100 m high waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang-Bomdila highway, originating from Sela Pass slopes. Features a small hydel plant at the base.
facts: Bollywood song from Koyla filmed nearby

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso in 1683. Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, located a few km from Tawang town.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: 40-foot-high stupa-style memorial dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features names of martyrs and offers panoramic views of Tawang town and valleys.

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4600 m on the India-China LAC, 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and Border Personnel Meeting point. Requires special Army permit.
facts: 14th Dalai Lama entered India via this route in 1959

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Large ancient Buddhist stupa near Zemithang, about 90 km from Tawang, modeled after Boudhanath in Nepal. Important pilgrimage site for Monpa people with circumambulation path and prayer wheels.
facts: About 100 ft high, largest in the area
Near Zemithang village, ~90 km from Tawang

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main base for exploring Tawang, perched at about 3000 m with Monpa culture, markets, and access to monasteries and high passes. Gateway for ILP holders.

name: Zemithang
description: Remote Monpa village near the Bhutan and Tibet borders, about 85-90 km from Tawang. Site of Dalai Lama's 1959 entry point, Gorsam Chorten, and wintering black-necked cranes. Offbeat cultural and nature destination.
facts: About 85-90 km west of Tawang via Lumla
First Indian entry point for 14th Dalai Lama in 1959
